description: Teacher metadata for every branch, by set: backward branches give the obstacle, why it blocks MAIN, the evidence the five questions collect (rationale) and whether the standard is exact or supporting; forward branches give the progression type, direct or nearest related, the new demand, and (FORWARD 2) how it builds on FORWARD 1. plus_standard is true when the branch's standard is a Common Core (+) standard; this happens in some core-strand sets (their FORWARD 2) as well as in the advanced strand. The same fields are in each set file under sections[].branch.

sets.target_skill: Rewrite expressions containing square roots of negative numbers in the form a + bi and name the real and imaginary parts

branches.skill: Simplify square roots of positive numbers
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot pull perfect-square factors out of a square root. Why it matters: √(-18) = √18 · i must then be simplified to 3√2 i. Evidence: simplifies square roots of positive integers.

branches.skill: No real number squares to a negative number
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see why a new number i is needed. Why it matters: i is defined so that i² = -1, which no real number satisfies. Evidence: states that squares of real numbers are never negative.

branches.skill: Divide each term of a sum by a number
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student divides only the first term of the numerator. Why it matters: writing (−4 + √(−75))/2 in a + bi form needs each part divided. Evidence: splits a quotient of a sum term by term.

branches.skill: Use equality of complex numbers to find unknown real values
branches.new_demand: Use the uniqueness of the form a + bi (equal real parts and equal imaginary parts) to solve for unknown real values.

branches.skill: Represent complex numbers as points in the complex plane
branches.new_demand: Represent a + bi geometrically as the point (a, b) and find its distance from 0.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the pair of real values (a, b) that determines a complex number becomes a point in a plane.

sets.target_skill: Add and subtract complex numbers by combining real parts and imaginary parts

branches.skill: Combine like terms
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot keep the two kinds of terms separate. Why it matters: complex addition is combining like terms, with i playing the role of x. Evidence: combines like terms with a variable.

branches.skill: Add and subtract integers and decimals
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student makes sign errors when subtracting. Why it matters: each part of a complex difference is a signed subtraction. Evidence: adds and subtracts signed numbers.

branches.skill: Write square roots of negative numbers with i
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot rewrite a radical with a negative radicand. Why it matters: some sums are given with √ of negatives. Evidence: writes √(-n) as bi.

branches.skill: Find real parameters that make a sum real or imaginary
branches.new_demand: Generalize with a parameter: find the values that make a sum or difference real or pure imaginary.

branches.skill: Add complex numbers as vectors in the complex plane
branches.new_demand: Interpret complex addition and subtraction geometrically (parallelogram rule, distance, midpoint).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the real and imaginary parts that FORWARD 1 controlled become coordinates of vectors that add.

sets.target_skill: Multiply complex numbers and simplify powers of i using i² = -1 and the distributive property

branches.skill: Multiply binomials
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot distribute a product of two binomials. Why it matters: a complex product is a binomial product followed by i² = -1. Evidence: multiplies binomials correctly.

branches.skill: Use i² = -1 and the cycle of powers of i
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student treats i² as i or forgets its sign. Why it matters: every complex product produces an i² term. Evidence: simplifies small powers of i.

branches.skill: Divide whole numbers to find a remainder
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot reduce a large power of i. Why it matters: iⁿ depends only on the remainder of n divided by 4. Evidence: finds remainders on division by 4.

branches.skill: Find a real parameter that makes a product real
branches.new_demand: Generalize products with a parameter and decide when a product is real or pure imaginary.

branches.skill: Divide complex numbers using conjugates
branches.new_demand: Use the real product of conjugates to divide complex numbers.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the parameter that made a product real becomes the conjugate that makes a denominator real.

sets.target_skill: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients and non-real solutions, giving exact solutions in a + bi form

branches.skill: Use the quadratic formula and the discriminant
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot set up the formula or misreads the coefficients. Why it matters: the solutions come from the formula. Evidence: computes discriminants and states the formula.

branches.skill: Write square roots of negative numbers with i
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student stops at "no real solution". Why it matters: the complex solutions are written with i. Evidence: writes √ of a negative and splits the fraction.

branches.skill: Solve equations of the form (x - h)² = k
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student forgets the ± when taking square roots. Why it matters: both conjugate solutions come from ±. Evidence: uses ± when solving by square roots.

branches.skill: Find a quadratic from one complex solution
branches.new_demand: Solve the inverse problem: build the quadratic from one complex solution using conjugate pairs.

branches.skill: Classify solutions for a family of quadratics
branches.new_demand: Classify the solution set of a parameterized family and write the solutions in terms of the parameter.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: from one quadratic determined by a solution to a whole family classified by its parameter.

sets.target_skill: Use polynomial identities to factor polynomials, including sums of squares, into linear factors with complex numbers

branches.skill: Factor a difference of squares
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see a² - b² as (a + b)(a - b). Why it matters: x² + 25 is x² - (5i)², a difference of squares. Evidence: factors differences of squares.

branches.skill: Multiply complex conjugates
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot check a factorization. Why it matters: a factorization is verified by multiplying back. Evidence: multiplies conjugate factors.

branches.skill: Solve quadratics with complex solutions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the complex zeros that give the factors. Why it matters: each zero r gives a factor x - r. Evidence: solves quadratics over the complex numbers.

branches.skill: Factor cubic and quartic polynomials over the complex numbers
branches.new_demand: Extend to degree 3 and 4: combine sum/difference-of-cubes or quadratic-form identities with complex factoring.

branches.skill: Write polynomials with real coefficients from complex zeros
branches.new_demand: Reverse the factoring: build polynomials from complex zeros and reason about degree with conjugate pairs.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: factoring into complex linear factors is read backward to construct polynomials from their zeros.

sets.target_skill: Use the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra to count the complex zeros of a polynomial (with multiplicity), and recognize the argument that shows it holds for quadratics

branches.skill: Find the degree of a polynomial
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the degree, especially of a product. Why it matters: the theorem counts zeros by degree. Evidence: finds degrees of polynomials and products.

branches.skill: Find zeros from factored form
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot read zeros from factors. Why it matters: counting zeros uses each factor. Evidence: finds zeros from factors.

branches.skill: Solve quadratics with complex solutions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find non-real zeros. Why it matters: complete zero lists include non-real zeros. Evidence: solves quadratics over the complex numbers.

branches.skill: Relate the complex zeros to the real x-intercepts of a graph
branches.new_demand: Connect the count of complex zeros to what a graph shows: real zeros as x-intercepts, the rest non-real.

branches.skill: Prove existence statements about real zeros
branches.new_demand: Prove existence and parity statements about real zeros from the theorem and conjugate pairs.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the counts read from graphs are turned into general proofs about how many real zeros are possible.

sets.target_skill: Interpret terms, factors, coefficients, and bases of polynomial, rational, and exponential expressions in terms of a context

branches.skill: Name terms, factors, and coefficients
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot tell terms from factors. Why it matters: an interpretation depends on how a part combines with the rest. Evidence: names terms, factors, and coefficients.

branches.skill: Translate between a percent change and a multiplying factor
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student reads 0.97 as "97% growth". Why it matters: exponential bases are percent-change factors. Evidence: converts between factors and percent changes.

branches.skill: Interpret a quotient as an amount per unit
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot read a denominator as "per item". Why it matters: rational expressions in context are often averages or rates. Evidence: interprets quotients as unit rates.

branches.skill: Build an expression whose parts have given meanings
branches.new_demand: Reverse the task: compose an expression whose terms, factors, and bases carry stated meanings.

branches.skill: Rewrite an exponential expression to reveal a different rate
branches.new_demand: Use properties of exponents to rewrite the expression so that a different part (a rate per new time unit) appears.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: after building expressions from meanings, rewrite them so new meanings can be read from their parts.

sets.target_skill: Reason about the value of a complicated expression by treating one of its parts as a single quantity (its sign, size, or limits)

branches.skill: Squares are never negative
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know that a squared part has a minimum of 0. Why it matters: bounds come from the sign of the squared part. Evidence: states the minimum of squared expressions.

branches.skill: Powers of numbers greater than 1 and between 0 and 1
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compare a power with 1. Why it matters: the factor (1 + r)ⁿ or (0.8)ᵗ is judged by comparing with 1. Evidence: compares powers with 1.

branches.skill: A fraction gets smaller as its denominator grows
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot bound a quotient. Why it matters: rational parts are bounded by bounding their denominators. Evidence: compares fractions with equal numerators.

branches.skill: Find the set of all values of an expression on a domain
branches.new_demand: Use the single-entity view to find every value (the range) an expression takes on a stated domain.

branches.skill: Use single-entity reasoning to find horizontal asymptotes
branches.new_demand: Use the behavior of one part for large inputs to find and justify horizontal asymptotes of rational functions.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the bounds found there become end behavior (asymptotes) of the graph.

sets.target_skill: Factor polynomials completely over the integers by seeing them as differences of squares or sums or differences of cubes

branches.skill: Take out a greatest common factor
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student skips the common factor. Why it matters: factoring completely starts by removing it. Evidence: takes out greatest common factors.

branches.skill: Recognize perfect squares and perfect cubes
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see the squares and cubes inside an expression. Why it matters: every pattern needs a = ... and b = .... Evidence: writes monomials as squares and cubes.

branches.skill: Multiply to check a factoring pattern
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misremembers the cube patterns. Why it matters: multiplying back confirms the pattern and the signs. Evidence: multiplies the pattern factors.

branches.skill: Factor expressions whose parts are themselves expressions
branches.new_demand: Apply the patterns when a or b is itself an expression (a binomial treated as one quantity).

branches.skill: Complete the factorization over the complex numbers
branches.new_demand: Carry the integer factorization further into linear factors over the complex numbers.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the structure-based factorizations are completed with complex linear factors.

sets.target_skill: Recognize an expression in quadratic form, substitute a single variable for the repeated part, and factor completely

branches.skill: Factor quadratic trinomials
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot factor the quadratic after the substitution. Why it matters: the substitution turns the problem into a trinomial. Evidence: factors trinomials.

branches.skill: Write powers as squares of other powers
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see x⁴ or 9ˣ as a square. Why it matters: quadratic form needs the leading part to be the square of the middle part. Evidence: rewrites powers as squares.

branches.skill: Treat a repeated part as a single variable
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see the repeated part. Why it matters: the substitution is the structure that makes the expression quadratic. Evidence: chooses and uses a substitution.

branches.skill: Solve equations in quadratic form over the complex numbers
branches.new_demand: Use the quadratic-form factorization to solve higher-degree equations, including non-real solutions.

branches.skill: Solve exponential equations in quadratic form
branches.new_demand: Reject impossible values (an exponential is always positive) and finish with logarithms.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the same substitution, now with an exponential part whose values are restricted to positive numbers.

sets.target_skill: Derive the sum of a finite geometric series by multiplying by the common ratio and subtracting, with r ≠ 1: choose the correct step, result, or reason in the derivation

branches.skill: Write terms of a geometric sequence
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot identify a, r, and the last term. Why it matters: the derivation uses the general term. Evidence: writes terms of geometric sequences.

branches.skill: Distribute a factor over a sum
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot multiply a whole series by r. Why it matters: the method multiplies every term by r. Evidence: distributes and subtracts lists of terms.

branches.skill: Use the product rule for exponents
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot simplify the shifted last term. Why it matters: the subtraction leaves arⁿ. Evidence: multiplies powers with the same base.

branches.skill: Prove the sum formula from a polynomial identity
branches.new_demand: Derive the same formula a second way, as a consequence of a proved polynomial identity.

branches.skill: Describe how partial sums behave when the ratio is between -1 and 1
branches.new_demand: Use the derived formula as a parameter statement to reason about how partial sums behave as n grows (no limit proof required).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the proved formula is now used to reason about families of partial sums.

sets.target_skill: Identify a, r, and n in a situation and use Sₙ = a(1 - rⁿ)/(1 - r) to find a total

branches.skill: Identify the first term, ratio, and number of terms
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misidentifies a, r, or n (often n off by one). Why it matters: the formula needs all three exactly. Evidence: reads a, r, and n from series.

branches.skill: Change a percent to a growth factor
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student uses the percent instead of the factor. Why it matters: the ratio is a factor such as 1.005. Evidence: converts percents to factors.

branches.skill: Round results of calculations correctly
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student rounds too early or too coarsely. Why it matters: money answers need the nearest cent. Evidence: rounds at the end to a stated precision.

branches.skill: Find the number of terms with logarithms
branches.new_demand: Solve the inverse problem: find the number of terms needed for a target sum, using logarithms.

branches.skill: Compare two payment plans with the series formula
branches.new_demand: Compare two models and find a break-even point by checking consecutive whole numbers.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: solving for the number of terms becomes finding when one total overtakes another.

sets.target_skill: Add and subtract polynomials of degree 3 or more and write the result in standard form

branches.skill: Combine like terms with the same power
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student combines unlike powers. Why it matters: addition of polynomials combines only like terms. Evidence: combines like terms by power.

branches.skill: Subtract a whole expression
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student changes only the first sign when subtracting. Why it matters: a difference subtracts every term. Evidence: distributes a minus sign.

branches.skill: Write polynomials in standard form
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot organize the result. Why it matters: answers must be in standard form. Evidence: orders terms by degree.

branches.skill: Reason about the degree of a sum or difference
branches.new_demand: Reason with a parameter about closure and the degree of a sum or difference.

branches.skill: Add and subtract rational expressions
branches.new_demand: Move from the polynomial system to the rational-expression system, where division is allowed.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: closure of polynomials under addition and subtraction contrasts with the need for rational expressions under division.

sets.target_skill: Multiply polynomials whose product has degree 3 or more and write the product in standard form

branches.skill: Distribute a monomial over a polynomial
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misses terms when distributing. Why it matters: each product of polynomials is a sum of monomial products. Evidence: distributes monomials.

branches.skill: Multiply powers with the same base
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student multiplies exponents instead of adding them. Why it matters: every term product uses the product rule. Evidence: multiplies powers.

branches.skill: Multiply two binomials
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot multiply the first two factors. Why it matters: three-factor products start with a binomial product. Evidence: multiplies binomials.

branches.skill: Find a coefficient of a product without full expansion
branches.new_demand: Use the structure of a product to find one coefficient or a parameter without expanding fully.

branches.skill: Expand powers of binomials with the Binomial Theorem
branches.new_demand: Replace repeated multiplication with the Binomial Theorem pattern.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: counting which term products give a coefficient leads to the binomial coefficients.

sets.target_skill: Find the remainder when a polynomial p(x) is divided by x - a by evaluating p(a)

branches.skill: Evaluate a polynomial function
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot evaluate p(a) accurately. Why it matters: the remainder is p(a). Evidence: evaluates polynomials at given inputs.

branches.skill: Powers of negative numbers
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student makes sign errors with negative inputs. Why it matters: dividing by x + 2 means evaluating at -2. Evidence: evaluates powers of negatives.

branches.skill: Dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what a remainder is. Why it matters: the theorem states the remainder of a division. Evidence: relates dividend, divisor, quotient, and remainder.

branches.skill: Find unknown coefficients from given remainders
branches.new_demand: Solve the inverse problem: use given remainders to find unknown coefficients.

branches.skill: Prove the Remainder Theorem
branches.new_demand: Prove the theorem from the division identity and connect it to factors.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the evaluations used to find unknowns are justified by a general proof.

sets.target_skill: Use p(a) = 0 to decide whether x - a is a factor of a polynomial, and use the factor to factor the polynomial completely

branches.skill: Use the Remainder Theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot test a candidate factor. Why it matters: x - a is a factor exactly when p(a) = 0. Evidence: computes remainders by evaluation.

branches.skill: Factor the quadratic quotient
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student stops after finding one factor. Why it matters: factoring completely needs the quotient factored. Evidence: factors quadratics.

branches.skill: Divide a polynomial by a linear factor
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the other factor. Why it matters: after x - a, the quotient carries the rest of the factorization. Evidence: finds and checks quotients.

branches.skill: Choose parameters so that a given binomial is a factor
branches.new_demand: Use the factor condition p(a) = 0 as an equation to find unknown coefficients.

branches.skill: Finish factorizations over the complex numbers
branches.new_demand: Use the factor found with the factor theorem, then finish the factorization with complex linear factors.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: after placing real factors, the remaining quadratic is factored over the complex numbers.

sets.target_skill: Factor a polynomial when needed and list every real zero with its multiplicity

branches.skill: Solve by the zero-product property
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot get zeros from factors. Why it matters: zeros are where a factor is 0. Evidence: uses the zero-product property.

branches.skill: Factor to find hidden repeated factors
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot see the factorization. Why it matters: multiplicities only show in factored form. Evidence: factors perfect squares and differences of squares.

branches.skill: An exponent counts repeated factors
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not connect exponents with multiplicity. Why it matters: the multiplicity is the exponent of the factor. Evidence: reads exponents as repeated factors.

branches.skill: Build a polynomial from zeros and one more condition
branches.new_demand: Construct a polynomial from roots, multiplicities, and a scale condition (an inverse problem).

branches.skill: Decide what the zeros determine and what remains free
branches.new_demand: Justify which conditions (degree, scale, multiplicities, non-real zeros) are needed for a polynomial to be determined.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: after building a polynomial from given conditions, analyze which conditions were necessary and what stays free.

sets.target_skill: Use the zeros, their multiplicities, the leading term, and the y-intercept to identify the rough graph of a factored polynomial among graphs that differ in one of these features

branches.skill: Read zeros and multiplicities
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot list the zeros. Why it matters: a rough graph is anchored at its zeros. Evidence: reads zeros and multiplicities.

branches.skill: End behavior from the leading term
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student draws the ends the wrong way. Why it matters: end behavior follows the leading term. Evidence: finds leading terms and their end behavior.

branches.skill: Find the y-intercept by evaluating at 0
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student has no point to check the sketch. Why it matters: the y-intercept and a test value fix the shape. Evidence: evaluates at 0 and at test points.

branches.skill: Sign of a power of a negative or positive number
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot tell crossing from touching. Why it matters: an odd power changes sign at the zero and an even power does not. Evidence: finds signs of powers.

branches.skill: Sketch graphs from standard form by factoring first
branches.new_demand: Start from standard form: find a suitable factorization before sketching.

branches.skill: Write a polynomial from its rough graph
branches.new_demand: Invert the sketch: recover a polynomial (zeros, multiplicities, scale) from graph features and test consistency.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the features drawn from a factorization are now read back to write the factorization.

sets.target_skill: Prove a polynomial identity: identify the valid argument that transforms one side into the other, and reject example checks and invalid algebra

branches.skill: Expand the square of a binomial
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student expands squares incorrectly. Why it matters: every identity proof here starts with expansion. Evidence: expands binomial powers.

branches.skill: Recognize a difference of squares
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student only expands. Why it matters: structure gives shorter proofs. Evidence: sees u² - v².

branches.skill: What makes an identity
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student proves by checking examples. Why it matters: a proof must work for all values. Evidence: distinguishes identities from equations.

branches.skill: Prove or disprove proposed identities
branches.new_demand: Decide whether a proposed identity is true; prove it or produce a counterexample, including with a parameter.

branches.skill: Prove identities with the Binomial Theorem
branches.new_demand: Use a general identity (the Binomial Theorem) and substitution to prove families of numerical facts.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: after proving single identities, a general identity is specialized to prove new ones.

sets.target_skill: Use a polynomial identity to generate or compute numerical relationships

branches.skill: Substitute values into an identity
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot evaluate the expressions. Why it matters: using an identity means substituting numbers. Evidence: evaluates expressions.

branches.skill: Check a Pythagorean triple
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what a triple is. Why it matters: the identity is used to produce triples. Evidence: checks a² + b² = c².

branches.skill: Choose a and b to fit a product
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot match a product to the pattern. Why it matters: the identity applies only after choosing a and b. Evidence: rewrites products as (a - b)(a + b).

branches.skill: Generate a triple with a required side
branches.new_demand: Work backward from a desired numerical relationship to the inputs of the identity.

branches.skill: Connect the triple identity to complex numbers
branches.new_demand: See the same identity inside complex-number multiplication.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: choosing x and y for the identity is the same as choosing the complex number x + yi to square.

sets.target_skill: Expand (x + y)ⁿ or find one of its terms using the Binomial Theorem and the binomial coefficients

branches.skill: Multiply binomials repeatedly
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot expand small powers. Why it matters: the theorem summarizes repeated multiplication. Evidence: expands small binomial powers.

branches.skill: Build Pascal's Triangle by a rule
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot get the coefficients. Why it matters: the binomial coefficients are the rows of the triangle. Evidence: generates rows by the rule.

branches.skill: Powers of products and of negatives
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student forgets to raise the coefficient or sign. Why it matters: each term includes powers like (2a)ᵏ and (-2y)ᵏ. Evidence: raises products to powers.

branches.skill: Find a specific term or coefficient with a condition
branches.new_demand: Choose the right term index under a condition (constant term, given coefficient) instead of expanding fully.

branches.skill: Use binomial coefficients to compute probabilities
branches.new_demand: Interpret the terms of (p + q)ⁿ as probabilities of outcomes in repeated trials.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: selecting one term of a binomial expansion becomes computing the probability of one count of successes.

sets.target_skill: Rewrite a(x)/b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x) using long or synthetic division, and identify the correct result among the results of common division errors

branches.skill: Write a division with a remainder as a mixed number
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what the form q + r/b means. Why it matters: the polynomial form imitates mixed numbers. Evidence: rewrites improper fractions.

branches.skill: Multiply to check a division
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot verify a quotient. Why it matters: a = b·q + r is checked by multiplication. Evidence: multiplies and adds the remainder.

branches.skill: Use the Remainder Theorem to check the remainder
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student makes arithmetic slips in division. Why it matters: p(a) checks the remainder independently. Evidence: evaluates at the divisor's zero.

branches.skill: Divide with unknown coefficients and higher-degree divisors
branches.new_demand: Use the division form a = bq + r with unknowns and quadratic divisors.

branches.skill: Use division to find slant asymptotes
branches.new_demand: Interpret the quotient q(x) as the end behavior (asymptote) of the rational function.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the division form a/b = q + r/b is read graphically, with r/b → 0.

sets.target_skill: Rewrite a simple rational expression in the form q(x) + r/b(x) by inspection, without long division

branches.skill: Split a fraction with a sum in the numerator
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student splits the denominator. Why it matters: inspection splits the numerator over the denominator. Evidence: splits numerators correctly.

branches.skill: Rewrite a numerator as a multiple of the denominator plus a constant
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the constant. Why it matters: inspection requires rewriting the numerator. Evidence: matches a multiple of the denominator.

branches.skill: Divide by long division when inspection fails
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student has no method to check. Why it matters: long division confirms the inspection. Evidence: divides polynomials.

branches.skill: Use the rewritten form to reason about values
branches.new_demand: Use the q + r/b form to reason about integer values, impossible values, and bounds.

branches.skill: Graph rational functions as transformations of y = 1/x
branches.new_demand: Read the inspected form as a transformation and locate the asymptotes.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the constant q and the term r/b found by inspection become a vertical shift and a shifted hyperbola.

sets.target_skill: Multiply and divide rational expressions, simplify, and state every excluded value of the original expression

branches.skill: Multiply and divide fractions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student forgets to invert the divisor. Why it matters: rational expressions follow fraction rules. Evidence: multiplies and divides fractions.

branches.skill: Factor numerators and denominators
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cancels terms instead of factors. Why it matters: only common factors cancel. Evidence: factors completely.

branches.skill: Division by zero is undefined
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student drops excluded values after simplifying. Why it matters: the simplified form must keep the original domain. Evidence: finds where expressions are undefined.

branches.skill: Simplify complex fractions
branches.new_demand: Simplify nested rational expressions while tracking all excluded values.

branches.skill: Explain closure of rational expressions
branches.new_demand: Justify the structure: rational expressions form a system like the rational numbers.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the simplifications of complex fractions rely on the reciprocal rule, which proves closure under division.

sets.target_skill: Add and subtract rational expressions using a common denominator, simplify, and state every excluded value

branches.skill: Add fractions with unlike denominators
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student adds denominators. Why it matters: rational expressions follow the fraction method. Evidence: uses a common denominator.

branches.skill: Find a least common denominator by factoring
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student multiplies all denominators. Why it matters: factoring gives the simplest common denominator. Evidence: finds LCDs.

branches.skill: Subtract a whole numerator
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student subtracts only the first term of the numerator. Why it matters: a difference of fractions subtracts the whole numerator. Evidence: distributes subtraction.

branches.skill: Decompose into partial fractions
branches.new_demand: Reverse the addition: split a rational expression into a sum of simpler ones and use it.

branches.skill: Solve rational equations
branches.new_demand: Use combined rational expressions to solve equations and reject excluded values.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: combining and splitting rational expressions is now used to solve equations.

sets.target_skill: Write a one-variable rational, radical, or exponential equation for a context and solve it

branches.skill: Express rates of work and unit rates
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student adds times instead of rates. Why it matters: the work equation adds rates 1/t. Evidence: writes rates as fractions.

branches.skill: Write exponential growth models
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write the growth model. Why it matters: the exponential equation comes from the model. Evidence: writes exponential models.

branches.skill: Solve linear equations after clearing a denominator
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot finish the algebra. Why it matters: each model reduces to a linear equation. Evidence: solves linear equations.

branches.skill: Create equations whose algebraic solutions must be checked against the context
branches.new_demand: Create equations whose algebraic solutions include ones the context rules out.

branches.skill: Solve exponential context equations with logarithms
branches.new_demand: Solve context equations whose solutions need logarithms.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the same create-solve-check cycle now ends with an exact logarithmic solution.

sets.target_skill: Write a one-variable polynomial, rational, or exponential inequality for a context, solve it, and interpret the solution

branches.skill: Solve quadratic equations by factoring
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the boundary values. Why it matters: the inequality changes at the solutions of the equation. Evidence: solves by factoring.

branches.skill: Sign of a product on intervals
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student picks the wrong side of the boundaries. Why it matters: the solution set is where the expression has the right sign. Evidence: tests signs of products.

branches.skill: Reverse the inequality when multiplying by a negative
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student keeps the inequality direction. Why it matters: every step must keep the solution set. Evidence: reverses inequality direction correctly.

branches.skill: Solve rational inequalities with sign charts and excluded values
branches.new_demand: Solve rational inequalities where the sign of a denominator changes, including excluded values.

branches.skill: Write systems of constraints and judge viability
branches.new_demand: Combine several nonlinear constraints and decide which solutions are viable.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: solution sets of single inequalities are intersected with further constraints.

sets.target_skill: Write a two-variable nonlinear equation for a context and identify the correct equation together with its correct graph on scaled axes

branches.skill: Make a table of values from an equation
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student has no points to plot. Why it matters: graphs are drawn from computed values. Evidence: computes tables from equations.

branches.skill: Choose scales and label axes
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot fit the graph on the grid. Why it matters: the standard requires labels and scales. Evidence: chooses scales and labels.

branches.skill: Write a growth or decay model from a percent
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write the exponential equation. Why it matters: two of the models are exponential. Evidence: writes exponential models.

branches.skill: Create equations in more than two variables and graph a member of the family
branches.new_demand: Create equations with more than two variables and graph members of the family.

branches.skill: Interpret key features of the created models
branches.new_demand: Interpret intercepts, asymptotic behavior, and changing rates of the models in context.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: after creating and graphing models, their key features are interpreted.

sets.target_skill: Represent constraints in a context with nonlinear equations or inequalities and decide whether options are viable

branches.skill: Represent constraints with a linear system
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot translate the words. Why it matters: nonlinear constraints use the same translations. Evidence: writes linear constraints.

branches.skill: Test whether a point satisfies an inequality
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot test an option. Why it matters: viability is decided by substitution. Evidence: tests values in inequalities.

branches.skill: Solve quadratic inequalities
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the viable range. Why it matters: the viable set is the solution of the nonlinear inequality. Evidence: solves quadratic inequalities.

branches.skill: Optimize within nonlinear constraints
branches.new_demand: Find the best viable option and list all viable options under several nonlinear constraints.

branches.skill: Locate constraint boundaries as graph intersections
branches.new_demand: Connect the boundary values of constraints to intersections of graphs.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the optimal and boundary values found algebraically are read from graph intersections.

sets.target_skill: Rearrange a rational, radical, or exponential formula to isolate a quantity, and state the conditions used

branches.skill: Rearrange linear formulas
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot isolate a variable. Why it matters: the same reasoning applies to nonlinear formulas. Evidence: rearranges linear formulas.

branches.skill: Undo squares and square roots
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not undo the radical. Why it matters: radical formulas are rearranged by squaring. Evidence: undoes squares and roots.

branches.skill: Clear fractions in an equation
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot clear denominators. Why it matters: rational formulas need reciprocals or cross-multiplication. Evidence: clears fractions.

branches.skill: Rearrange formulas where conditions decide the result
branches.new_demand: Track the conditions (sign, excluded values) that the rearranged formula must keep.

branches.skill: Rearrange exponential formulas with logarithms
branches.new_demand: Isolate a variable in an exponent with logarithms.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: rearranging with conditions now includes undoing an exponential with a logarithm (A/P > 0).

sets.target_skill: Solve a rational equation in one variable, check every candidate, and identify extraneous solutions

branches.skill: Solve proportions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot clear a single fraction. Why it matters: rational equations reduce to proportions. Evidence: solves proportions.

branches.skill: Find a common denominator of rational expressions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student multiplies by the wrong expression. Why it matters: clearing denominators uses the LCD. Evidence: finds LCDs.

branches.skill: Values that make a denominator zero
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student keeps excluded values. Why it matters: extraneous solutions are excluded values produced by clearing. Evidence: lists excluded values.

branches.skill: Explain and construct extraneous solutions
branches.new_demand: Explain why extraneous solutions arise and construct equations with prescribed solution behavior.

branches.skill: See rational equations as graph intersections
branches.new_demand: Interpret solutions, non-solutions, and extraneous values with graphs.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the algebraic explanation of extraneous values is matched to graphs that are undefined there.

sets.target_skill: Solve a radical equation in one variable, check every candidate, and identify extraneous solutions

branches.skill: Square and cube both sides; principal roots
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student squares incorrectly or allows negative roots. Why it matters: solving begins by undoing the root. Evidence: undoes roots and knows principal roots.

branches.skill: Solve the resulting quadratic
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot finish after squaring. Why it matters: squaring produces a quadratic. Evidence: solves quadratics.

branches.skill: Check a candidate in the original equation
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not check. Why it matters: squaring can introduce extraneous solutions. Evidence: checks candidates.

branches.skill: Solve equations with two radicals, rational exponents, and √(x²)
branches.new_demand: Solve radical equations needing two squarings, rational exponents, or the absolute value √(x²) = |x|.

branches.skill: Explain extraneous solutions with graphs of radical functions
branches.new_demand: Explain extraneous and missing solutions with the graphs of radical functions.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the algebraic role of squaring (and of |x|) is seen as merging the graphs of √ and -√.

sets.target_skill: Explain why the x-coordinates of the intersections of y = f(x) and y = g(x) solve f(x) = g(x), for polynomial, rational, radical, absolute value, and exponential functions

branches.skill: A graph is the set of its solutions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see a graph as a solution set. Why it matters: the explanation depends on this meaning. Evidence: tests points on graphs.

branches.skill: Solve a linear system by graphing
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student has no model of intersection meaning. Why it matters: the nonlinear case extends the linear one. Evidence: reads linear intersections.

branches.skill: Evaluate nonlinear functions at an input
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot verify a solution. Why it matters: a read solution is confirmed by evaluating both sides. Evidence: evaluates functions.

branches.skill: Relate intersections to zeros of f - g
branches.new_demand: Move between intersections of two graphs and zeros of a single difference function.

branches.skill: Find all solutions of a trigonometric equation on an interval from a graph
branches.new_demand: Apply the intersection idea to periodic functions, where every solution on an interval must be found.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: counting intersections and sign changes now handles periodic graphs with repeated solutions.

sets.target_skill: Approximate the solutions of f(x) = g(x) with tables, graphs, or successive approximation, to a stated accuracy

branches.skill: Read solutions of linear-quadratic systems from graphs
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot read intersections. Why it matters: approximations start from a graph or table. Evidence: reads solutions of simple systems.

branches.skill: Evaluate exponential and logarithmic expressions with a calculator
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute table entries. Why it matters: tables need accurate values. Evidence: evaluates with technology.

branches.skill: Round to a place value
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student reports the wrong precision. Why it matters: answers are required to a stated accuracy. Evidence: rounds decimals.

branches.skill: Guarantee the accuracy of an approximation
branches.new_demand: Justify the accuracy of an approximation with sign changes and interval halving.

branches.skill: Compare an approximation with an exact logarithmic solution
branches.new_demand: Decide when an exact logarithmic solution exists and when only approximation works.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the guaranteed approximation is compared with an exact logarithmic solution.

sets.target_skill: Interpret and find radian measures as arc lengths on the unit circle, and convert between degrees and radians

branches.skill: Circumference of a circle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the length of the unit circle. Why it matters: radian measure is arc length on that circle. Evidence: computes circumferences.

branches.skill: Arc length is proportional to the angle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot relate angle to arc. Why it matters: radian measure is defined from the arc. Evidence: uses proportional arcs.

branches.skill: Degrees as fractions of a turn
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot convert. Why it matters: conversions use the same fraction of a turn. Evidence: writes angles as fractions of a turn.

branches.skill: Measure negative angles and angles beyond one turn
branches.new_demand: Extend radian measure to negative angles and angles greater than one turn.

branches.skill: Read sine and cosine of radian angles from the unit circle
branches.new_demand: Use the endpoint of the arc of any radian length to define cosine and sine.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: angles of any size locate a point on the unit circle, whose coordinates are cos and sin.

sets.target_skill: Use the unit circle, reference angles, and quadrant signs to find exact values of sine, cosine, and tangent for any angle

branches.skill: Special right triangle ratios
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the first-quadrant values. Why it matters: values in other quadrants come from them. Evidence: gives special ratios.

branches.skill: Reference angles for radian measures
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot locate the angle. Why it matters: the reference angle and quadrant give the value. Evidence: finds reference angles.

branches.skill: Signs of coordinates by quadrant
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student uses the wrong sign. Why it matters: cos and sin are the coordinates. Evidence: gives quadrant signs.

branches.skill: Values for angles beyond 2π and solving for angles
branches.new_demand: Work with angles beyond one turn and solve for all angles in an interval with a given value.

branches.skill: Verify the Pythagorean identity at exact values
branches.new_demand: Connect the exact values to the circle equation, the basis of the Pythagorean identity.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: values for every quadrant are checked against x² + y² = 1.

sets.target_skill: Explain how the unit circle defines sine and cosine for every real number, using radian measures traversed counterclockwise or clockwise: identify the correct explanation and reject flawed ones

branches.skill: Right-triangle definitions of sine and cosine
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student only knows triangle definitions. Why it matters: the unit circle extends them. Evidence: states triangle definitions and their limits.

branches.skill: Points on the unit circle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the circle's equation. Why it matters: bounds and the identity follow from it. Evidence: uses x² + y² = 1.

branches.skill: Radian measure as directed arc length
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot locate the endpoint. Why it matters: the definition uses arc length and direction. Evidence: locates endpoints of arcs.

branches.skill: Explain where tangent is defined and how values repeat
branches.new_demand: Explain domains, ranges, and undefined values that the unit-circle definition creates.

branches.skill: Explain symmetry and periodicity
branches.new_demand: Use reflections and rotations of the unit circle to explain symmetry and periodicity.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the explanation of cos(-t) = cos t is generalized to odd/even symmetry and periods.

sets.target_skill: Choose a sine or cosine function with the specified amplitude, frequency or period, and midline to model a periodic situation

branches.skill: Amplitude and midline from the maximum and minimum
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot get A and D from the context. Why it matters: the parameters come from the extremes. Evidence: computes midpoint and half-range.

branches.skill: Period and frequency
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student confuses period and frequency. Why it matters: models are specified by either. Evidence: relates period and frequency.

branches.skill: Vertical stretches, shifts, and reflections
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot place A and D. Why it matters: the model is a transformed sine or cosine. Evidence: applies vertical transformations.

branches.skill: Write models from data or with a phase shift
branches.new_demand: Determine every parameter, including a horizontal shift, from data points.

branches.skill: Solve for times in sinusoidal models
branches.new_demand: Use the built model and inverse reasoning to find every time a value occurs.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: after fitting the parameters, the model is solved for times.

sets.target_skill: Interpret amplitude, period, frequency, and midline of a sinusoidal model in context and use them to answer questions

branches.skill: Build the model from amplitude, period, and midline
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot read A, B, D. Why it matters: interpretation starts from the parameters. Evidence: identifies parameters.

branches.skill: Evaluate a sinusoidal model
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute extremes. Why it matters: max and min come from sin = ±1. Evidence: evaluates trigonometric expressions.

branches.skill: Convert rates between units
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot answer per-minute questions. Why it matters: contexts mix time units. Evidence: converts rates.

branches.skill: Predict how changing a parameter changes the situation
branches.new_demand: Reason about how a change in context changes one parameter of the model.

branches.skill: Interpret periodic features from graphs and tables
branches.new_demand: Read the same periodic features from graphs and tables instead of formulas.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: parameter changes in a formula are now recognized as features of a graph or table.

sets.target_skill: Prove sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and closely related identities: identify the valid argument and reject example checks and invalid steps

branches.skill: The Pythagorean Theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the theorem. Why it matters: the identity is the theorem on the unit circle. Evidence: uses the Pythagorean Theorem.

branches.skill: Coordinates of the point at angle θ
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot name the point. Why it matters: the proof substitutes these coordinates. Evidence: names unit-circle points.

branches.skill: Expand and simplify algebraic squares
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot manipulate the identity. Why it matters: derived identities need algebra. Evidence: expands and divides expressions.

branches.skill: Prove identities derived from the Pythagorean identity
branches.new_demand: Use the proved identity as a tool to prove new identities.

branches.skill: Use the angle-addition formulas
branches.new_demand: Extend from the Pythagorean identity to the sum and double-angle identities (Precalculus).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: identities like cos²θ - sin²θ = 2cos²θ - 1 reappear as double-angle formulas.

sets.target_skill: Given one trigonometric value and the quadrant, use sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 to find the other values with correct signs

branches.skill: Signs of sine, cosine, and tangent by quadrant
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student gives the wrong sign. Why it matters: the identity gives magnitudes; the quadrant gives signs. Evidence: gives signs by quadrant.

branches.skill: Square roots of fractions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot simplify the root. Why it matters: cos θ = ±√(1 - sin²θ). Evidence: simplifies square roots.

branches.skill: Solve x² = c
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student keeps only one root. Why it matters: two signs are possible before the quadrant is used. Evidence: solves x² = c.

branches.skill: Find values when the quadrant is not given, and combine values
branches.new_demand: Handle the ambiguity when the quadrant is unknown and chain the identity with other relations.

branches.skill: Find the angles with inverse trigonometric functions
branches.new_demand: Move from values to the angles themselves with inverse functions, choosing the correct quadrant.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the two quadrant cases for cos θ correspond to the two angles found with arcsin.

sets.target_skill: Interpret intercepts, intervals of increase and decrease, relative extrema, positive and negative intervals, and end behavior of polynomial and rational models in context

branches.skill: Interpret key features of linear and quadratic models
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot name key features. Why it matters: the same features are read from new families. Evidence: interprets linear and quadratic graphs.

branches.skill: Describe increasing and decreasing behavior
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student lacks the vocabulary. Why it matters: interpretation is in words. Evidence: describes behavior qualitatively.

branches.skill: Zeros and sign from factors
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot locate intercepts. Why it matters: intercepts and signs come from factors. Evidence: finds zeros and signs.

branches.skill: Sketch a model from a verbal description of key features
branches.new_demand: Reverse the task: produce a graph or formula from a verbal list of key features.

branches.skill: Compare key features across representations
branches.new_demand: Compare features when the functions are given in different representations.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: features produced from descriptions are now compared across formulas, tables, and graphs.

sets.target_skill: Read the period, maximums, minimums, and intervals of increase of a periodic model from a graph or table and interpret them in context

branches.skill: Interpret maximums and minimums on a graph
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot read extremes. Why it matters: periodic features are maximums and minimums that repeat. Evidence: interprets extrema.

branches.skill: Read values from a table
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misreads tables. Why it matters: two items give data in tables. Evidence: reads tables.

branches.skill: Amplitude, period, and midline of a sinusoidal model
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot relate features to parameters. Why it matters: the features match the model's parameters. Evidence: reads parameters.

branches.skill: Predict with periodicity
branches.new_demand: Use the period to predict values far from the given data.

branches.skill: Write a model from periodic features
branches.new_demand: Translate the read features into a trigonometric model.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the period and extremes used for prediction become the parameters of a formula.

sets.target_skill: State the domain of a radical, rational, logarithmic, or polynomial function and the domain that makes sense in a context

branches.skill: Domains of linear, quadratic, and exponential models
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not separate function and context domains. Why it matters: both are required. Evidence: states context domains.

branches.skill: Division by zero
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student forgets excluded values. Why it matters: rational domains exclude zeros of denominators. Evidence: finds undefined inputs.

branches.skill: Solve linear inequalities
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find where a radicand or log input is valid. Why it matters: domain conditions are inequalities. Evidence: solves linear inequalities.

branches.skill: Domains defined by nonlinear conditions
branches.new_demand: Solve nonlinear inequalities (quadratic, combined conditions) to find domains.

branches.skill: Domains and ranges of inverse functions
branches.new_demand: Use domains and ranges to state the domain of an inverse function.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: domain conditions found by solving inequalities become the ranges and domains of inverses.

sets.target_skill: Calculate the average rate of change of a nonlinear function over an interval, from a formula or table, and interpret it with units

branches.skill: Average rate of change of simpler functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the formula. Why it matters: the same formula applies to new families. Evidence: computes average rates.

branches.skill: Slope between two points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute a slope. Why it matters: average rate is the slope of a secant line. Evidence: finds slopes.

branches.skill: Evaluate nonlinear functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot get the endpoints. Why it matters: the rate needs both outputs. Evidence: evaluates functions.

branches.skill: Compare average rates on different intervals
branches.new_demand: Compare rates across intervals to describe how a nonlinear model changes.

branches.skill: Compare rates of change across representations
branches.new_demand: Compute and compare average rates when functions are given differently.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: comparing rates on intervals is extended to comparing two functions in different representations.

sets.target_skill: Identify the graph of a transformed square root or cube root function from its starting point or center, key points, domain, and range

branches.skill: Graph y = √x and y = ∛x from a table
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the parent graphs. Why it matters: each graph transforms a parent graph. Evidence: graphs parent radical functions.

branches.skill: Translations and reflections of graphs
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot move key points. Why it matters: transformations locate the graph. Evidence: applies shifts and reflections.

branches.skill: Square and cube roots of numbers
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute points. Why it matters: plotted points need roots. Evidence: evaluates roots.

branches.skill: Graph radical functions with horizontal stretches and reflections
branches.new_demand: Include horizontal reflections and stretches f(-x), f(kx) of radical graphs.

branches.skill: Graph a radical function and its inverse
branches.new_demand: Relate the radical graph to its inverse and its restricted domain.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the starting points and domains of radical graphs become ranges and domains of inverses.

sets.target_skill: Identify the graphs of piecewise-defined functions (with open and closed endpoints) and of absolute value functions with transformations

branches.skill: Evaluate and graph simple piecewise functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student uses the wrong piece. Why it matters: each input belongs to exactly one piece. Evidence: evaluates piecewise functions.

branches.skill: Absolute value as distance
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot evaluate absolute values. Why it matters: absolute value graphs need these values. Evidence: evaluates |x|.

branches.skill: Open and closed endpoints
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student draws the wrong endpoints. Why it matters: piecewise graphs need correct endpoints. Evidence: uses open and closed circles.

branches.skill: Write piecewise functions from graphs and contexts
branches.new_demand: Write piecewise rules from descriptions and choose parameters for continuity.

branches.skill: Describe absolute value graphs as transformations, and identify symmetry
branches.new_demand: Relate absolute value graphs to transformations and symmetry.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the piecewise form of |x - 3| shows the reflection that makes absolute value graphs V-shaped and symmetric.

sets.target_skill: Factor a polynomial given in standard form, then identify its graph from the zeros (crossing or touching), the y-intercept, a point in each interval, and end behavior

branches.skill: Factor out common factors and special products
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the zeros. Why it matters: graphing uses the factorization. Evidence: factors polynomials.

branches.skill: Crossing and touching from multiplicity
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student draws every zero the same. Why it matters: multiplicity decides crossing. Evidence: relates multiplicity to shape.

branches.skill: Evaluate polynomials at test points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot place the curve between zeros. Why it matters: test points fix the height and sign. Evidence: evaluates polynomials.

branches.skill: Locate relative extrema of polynomial graphs
branches.new_demand: Estimate the relative extrema that a factorization does not give, with tables or technology.

branches.skill: Interpret polynomial graphs in context
branches.new_demand: Restrict polynomial graphs to a context and interpret their features.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the located extrema and zeros are interpreted as maximum volume, break-even, and peak values.

sets.target_skill: Identify the graph of a transformed exponential function from its y-intercept, any x-intercept, the horizontal asymptote, and end behavior

branches.skill: Graph basic exponential functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the parent shapes. Why it matters: every graph transforms y = b^x. Evidence: graphs basic exponentials.

branches.skill: Zero and negative exponents
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot plot left-side points. Why it matters: points with negative x need negative exponents. Evidence: evaluates exponents.

branches.skill: Vertical and horizontal shifts and reflections
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student draws the asymptote at y = 0 always. Why it matters: shifts move the asymptote. Evidence: applies shifts.

branches.skill: Compare and describe exponential graphs
branches.new_demand: Explain equivalences between transformations and write functions from graph features.

branches.skill: Graph the inverse of an exponential function
branches.new_demand: Reflect exponential graphs over y = x to obtain logarithmic graphs.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: features of exponential graphs (asymptote, intercept) become the features of their inverses.

sets.target_skill: Identify the graph of a transformed logarithmic function from its vertical asymptote, x-intercept, key points, domain, and end behavior

branches.skill: Graph exponential functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot get points of the log. Why it matters: log points are exponential points swapped. Evidence: graphs exponentials.

branches.skill: Find inverses by swapping inputs and outputs
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see a log as an inverse. Why it matters: log graphs reflect exponential graphs. Evidence: swaps coordinates.

branches.skill: Shift and reflect graphs
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student puts the asymptote at x = 0 always. Why it matters: shifts move it. Evidence: applies shifts.

branches.skill: Graph logarithms with reflections that change the domain
branches.new_demand: Handle reflections and compositions that change the domain of a logarithmic graph.

branches.skill: Solve equations with logarithms
branches.new_demand: Use logarithms (read from graphs or computed) to solve exponential equations.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: reading x-intercepts and values from log graphs becomes solving exponential equations.

sets.target_skill: Identify the graph of a sine or cosine function with given parameters from its period, midline, amplitude, and key points on a radian axis

branches.skill: Unit-circle values at quarter turns
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot plot key points. Why it matters: graphs use quarter-period values. Evidence: gives unit-circle values.

branches.skill: Read amplitude, period, and midline from a formula
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot scale the graph. Why it matters: the parameters set the scale. Evidence: reads parameters.

branches.skill: Vertical stretches, shifts, and reflections
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot place the midline. Why it matters: shifts and reflections move key points. Evidence: applies vertical transformations.

branches.skill: Graph shifted sinusoids and the tangent function
branches.new_demand: Include horizontal shifts and the tangent graph with asymptotes.

branches.skill: Horizontal stretches f(kx) of trigonometric graphs
branches.new_demand: Connect the period to the horizontal transformation f(kx), including negative k.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: after horizontal shifts, horizontal stretches and reflections of trig graphs are analyzed.

sets.target_skill: Use properties of exponents to rewrite an exponential function so it shows the growth or decay rate per a different time unit, and interpret it

branches.skill: Read growth rates from exponential functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot read a rate from a factor. Why it matters: rewriting is only useful if the factor is interpreted. Evidence: reads rates.

branches.skill: Powers of powers and rational exponents
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot regroup exponents. Why it matters: rewriting uses (b^m)^n = b^(mn). Evidence: uses exponent rules.

branches.skill: Percent change and growth factors
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot convert factors to percents. Why it matters: each answer reports a percent rate. Evidence: converts factors and percents.

branches.skill: Compare growth offers by rewriting to the same time unit
branches.new_demand: Rewrite two models to a common unit and compare them.

branches.skill: Find doubling times and half-lives with logarithms
branches.new_demand: Solve for the time unit that gives a chosen factor (2 or 1/2) with logarithms.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: comparing factors on common units leads to finding the time for a given factor.

sets.target_skill: Compare a property (intercept, maximum, period, domain, asymptote, or growth) of two functions given in different representations

branches.skill: Compare linear, quadratic, and exponential functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student has no comparison method. Why it matters: the same comparisons extend to new families. Evidence: compares Algebra I functions.

branches.skill: Recognize a pattern in a table
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot identify a tabled function. Why it matters: the type predicts its properties. Evidence: classifies tables.

branches.skill: Domains, asymptotes, and periods of Algebra II families
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the property in one representation. Why it matters: each comparison needs the property in both. Evidence: finds properties.

branches.skill: Compare rates of change and long-run behavior across representations
branches.new_demand: Compare growth and long-run behavior, not only one value.

branches.skill: Build a difference function to compare
branches.new_demand: Combine the two functions into one new function that encodes the comparison.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the crossing point of f and g is the zero of their difference function.

sets.target_skill: Build a function for a context by adding, subtracting, multiplying, or dividing standard function types, and evaluate it

branches.skill: Combine linear and quadratic functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot combine simpler models. Why it matters: the same operations apply to new types. Evidence: combines linear and quadratic functions.

branches.skill: Multiply and subtract polynomials
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student makes algebra errors. Why it matters: combined models must be simplified. Evidence: operates on polynomials.

branches.skill: Evaluate exponential and trigonometric expressions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot evaluate the combined model. Why it matters: each item asks for a value. Evidence: evaluates functions.

branches.skill: Interpret the parts of a combined model
branches.new_demand: Interpret each component of a combined model and its long-run effect.

branches.skill: Compose functions in context
branches.new_demand: Combine functions by composition (output of one is the input of the other).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: after interpreting arithmetic combinations, a new combination (composition) is introduced.

sets.target_skill: Find h and k (or a) when the graph of g is f(x - h) + k or a·f(x) for a radical, exponential, cubic, absolute value, or logarithmic parent f

branches.skill: Shifts and stretches of linear and quadratic graphs
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student reverses horizontal shifts. Why it matters: the same rules apply to all families. Evidence: transforms quadratics.

branches.skill: Translate points in the plane
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot move key points. Why it matters: h and k are read from moved points. Evidence: translates points.

branches.skill: Key points of parent functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know which point to track. Why it matters: each parent has a key point to compare. Evidence: names key points.

branches.skill: Write transformed functions from descriptions and order of transformations
branches.new_demand: Write functions for sequences of transformations and track the effect of order.

branches.skill: Read sinusoid parameters as transformations
branches.new_demand: See the amplitude and midline of a sinusoidal model as a vertical stretch and shift.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: ordered stretches and shifts become the parameters A and D of a trigonometric model.

sets.target_skill: Describe and apply the effect of replacing f(x) by f(kx), including negative k, on graphs and points

branches.skill: Reflections and dilations of points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot move points horizontally. Why it matters: f(kx) moves points by x → x/k. Evidence: transforms points.

branches.skill: Solve kx = c for x
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student multiplies instead of dividing. Why it matters: the new input satisfies kx = old input. Evidence: solves kx = c.

branches.skill: Period of y = sin(Bx)
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot connect B to stretching. Why it matters: the period shows the horizontal scale factor. Evidence: finds periods.

branches.skill: Combine horizontal stretches with shifts
branches.new_demand: Separate the horizontal factor from the shift in f(kx - c).

branches.skill: Graph exponential and trigonometric functions with horizontal changes
branches.new_demand: Use f(kx) to graph exponential and trigonometric functions and interpret the base or period.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: combined horizontal changes are now drawn and interpreted for specific families.

sets.target_skill: Decide whether a function is even, odd, or neither from its expression (by computing f(-x)) or from its graph

branches.skill: Signs of powers of negatives
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student mishandles signs. Why it matters: f(-x) uses powers of -x. Evidence: simplifies powers of negatives.

branches.skill: Reflect points over the axes and the origin
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot read symmetry. Why it matters: even and odd are symmetries of graphs. Evidence: reflects points.

branches.skill: Substitute -x into an expression
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute f(-x). Why it matters: the test compares f(-x) with f(x). Evidence: substitutes -x.

branches.skill: Reason about sums and products of even and odd functions
branches.new_demand: Prove general facts about even and odd functions and use them.

branches.skill: Explain trigonometric symmetry with the unit circle
branches.new_demand: Explain the even/odd behavior of trigonometric functions with the unit circle.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the product and quotient facts give the symmetry of tan from that of sin and cos.

sets.target_skill: Solve f(x) = y for x to write the inverse of a radical, rational, cubic, exponential, or logarithmic function, and state its domain

branches.skill: Inverses of linear functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find any inverse. Why it matters: the same method applies to new families. Evidence: inverts linear functions.

branches.skill: Rearrange formulas with roots, powers, and fractions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot isolate x. Why it matters: finding inverses is rearranging. Evidence: rearranges nonlinear formulas.

branches.skill: Domain and range
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student omits the inverse's domain. Why it matters: the domain of f⁻¹ is the range of f. Evidence: finds domains and ranges.

branches.skill: Inverses that are their own inverse, and checking by points
branches.new_demand: Use symmetry about y = x and the one-to-one property to reason about inverses.

branches.skill: Verify inverses by composition
branches.new_demand: Prove the inverse relationship with compositions and domains.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: checking single points is replaced by a general composition check.

sets.target_skill: Solve ab^(ct) = d for t and write the solution exactly as a logarithm (base 2, 10, or e)

branches.skill: Isolate the exponential expression
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student takes logs too early. Why it matters: the exponential must be isolated first. Evidence: isolates the exponential.

branches.skill: Powers of 2, 3, and 10
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misses exact powers. Why it matters: some equations need no logarithm. Evidence: recognizes powers.

branches.skill: Logarithms as the inverse of exponentials
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write a logarithm. Why it matters: exact solutions are logarithms. Evidence: converts exponential and log forms.

branches.skill: Solve equations with different bases or variables on both sides
branches.new_demand: Use logarithm properties to solve equations with exponentials on both sides.

branches.skill: Use the inverse relationship to solve logarithmic equations
branches.new_demand: Use exponentials to undo logarithms and check domains.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the logarithm properties used to solve exponential equations are reversed to solve log equations.

sets.target_skill: Solve an exponential model for time, evaluate the logarithm with technology to a stated precision, and interpret the answer in context

branches.skill: Write exact logarithmic solutions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student has no expression to evaluate. Why it matters: technology evaluates the exact log form. Evidence: writes exact solutions.

branches.skill: Evaluate logarithms with a calculator
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot use the calculator correctly. Why it matters: answers require numerical values. Evidence: evaluates logarithms.

branches.skill: Choose an appropriate level of accuracy
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student reports an answer that does not fit the context. Why it matters: interpretation requires sensible precision. Evidence: chooses accuracy.

branches.skill: Analyze how parameters change the solution
branches.new_demand: Investigate how changes in the parameters change the logarithmic solution.

branches.skill: Rewrite models to show doubling time or half-life
branches.new_demand: Rewrite the model so the logarithmic time (doubling time or half-life) is a visible parameter.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the solution times studied for different parameters become parameters of a rewritten model.

sets.target_skill: Use the mean and standard deviation of a normal model, with the 68-95-99.7 rule or a table, to estimate a population percentage

branches.skill: Interpret mean and standard deviation
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot locate values in standard deviations. Why it matters: normal estimates depend on z-scores. Evidence: measures distance in standard deviations.

branches.skill: Describe the shape of a distribution
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the normal shape. Why it matters: the rule only fits mound-shaped data. Evidence: describes shapes.

branches.skill: Percents of a whole
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot combine percents. Why it matters: estimates add and split percents. Evidence: computes percents.

branches.skill: Find values from percentiles of a normal model
branches.new_demand: Reverse the estimate: find the value that corresponds to a given percent.

branches.skill: Use a normal model for a margin of error
branches.new_demand: Apply the 95% normal range to the sampling distribution of a statistic.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: finding cutoffs for 95% of a population becomes finding a 95% range for a statistic.

sets.target_skill: Decide from a graph or summary whether a normal model is appropriate for a data set, and justify the decision

branches.skill: Describe skewed, symmetric, bimodal, and uniform shapes
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot name a shape. Why it matters: the decision depends on the shape. Evidence: names distribution shapes.

branches.skill: Measures of center and spread for a data set
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot use summaries. Why it matters: one item is judged from numbers alone. Evidence: uses center and spread.

branches.skill: Groups combined in one data set
