branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see why two peaks occur. Why it matters: a normal model fits one population. Evidence: recognizes mixtures.

branches.skill: Check a normal model with the 68-95-99.7 rule
branches.new_demand: Use percents within 1 and 2 SDs as numerical evidence for or against normality.

branches.skill: Decide whether a probability model fits observed data
branches.new_demand: Move from judging a distribution's shape to judging a model's consistency with observed results.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: comparing observed percents with model percents is extended to simulated outcomes.

sets.target_skill: Identify the population, sample, parameter, and statistic in a study and explain what a random sample allows one to conclude

branches.skill: Samples and populations
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student confuses sample and population. Why it matters: inference goes from sample to population. Evidence: defines sample and population.

branches.skill: Draw inferences from random samples
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not use samples to estimate. Why it matters: the statistic estimates the parameter. Evidence: makes inferences from samples.

branches.skill: Compute sample proportions and means
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute the statistic. Why it matters: statistics are computed from the sample. Evidence: computes proportions and means.

branches.skill: Describe sampling variability
branches.new_demand: Separate the effects of chance variation and of bias on statistics.

branches.skill: Quantify variability with a margin of error
branches.new_demand: Attach a numerical margin of error to the statistic.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the variability of statistics described in words is now measured.

sets.target_skill: Use supplied simulation results to decide whether a probability model is consistent with an observed result

branches.skill: Probability as long-run relative frequency
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student expects exact results. Why it matters: judging requires knowing what is typical. Evidence: uses expected counts.

branches.skill: Use simulations of compound events
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what the histogram represents. Why it matters: decisions rest on simulated runs. Evidence: designs and reads simulations.

branches.skill: Relative frequency of a group of outcomes
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the simulated proportion. Why it matters: the decision compares a proportion to a cutoff. Evidence: computes percents.

branches.skill: Design a simulation to test a model
branches.new_demand: Design the simulation and justify the "as extreme" criterion.

branches.skill: Compare two treatments with a re-randomization simulation
branches.new_demand: Apply the same model-testing logic to a randomized experiment.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the designed simulation for one proportion becomes a shuffle of treatment labels.

sets.target_skill: Identify the type of study (sample survey, experiment, observational study) and state its purpose and what it can show

branches.skill: Statistical questions and data collection
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student has no vocabulary for studies. Why it matters: types are defined by how data are collected. Evidence: describes data collection.

branches.skill: Association is not causation
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student draws causal conclusions from associations. Why it matters: study type determines whether causation can be shown. Evidence: separates correlation and causation.

branches.skill: Random samples
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see the role of randomness. Why it matters: surveys rely on random samples. Evidence: describes random sampling.

branches.skill: Identify confounding and design flaws
branches.new_demand: Diagnose confounding and redesign studies to support causal claims.

branches.skill: Analyze the results of an experiment
branches.new_demand: Analyze experimental data with simulation to decide if the treatment effect is significant.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: after designing an experiment that can show causation, its results are tested.

sets.target_skill: Explain the difference between random sampling and random assignment and state what each allows a study to conclude

branches.skill: Study types and their purposes
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student confuses the two random processes. Why it matters: each random step allows a different conclusion. Evidence: names study types.

branches.skill: Choose a random sample
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot describe random selection. Why it matters: one of the two random steps. Evidence: chooses random samples.

branches.skill: Correlation and causation
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student overstates conclusions. Why it matters: causal claims need random assignment. Evidence: separates association and causation.

branches.skill: Improve an experimental design
branches.new_demand: Improve designs with control, blocking, blinding, and sampling.

branches.skill: Use re-randomization to judge a treatment difference
branches.new_demand: Use simulation to test the effect allowed by random assignment.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: a well-designed experiment is analyzed with re-randomization.

sets.target_skill: Use a sample proportion and the variability of simulated sample proportions to give an estimate with a margin of error, and interpret it

branches.skill: Statistics, parameters, and sampling variability
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student confuses statistic and parameter. Why it matters: the margin is about estimating the parameter. Evidence: identifies statistic and parameter.

branches.skill: Proportions and percents
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot form the interval. Why it matters: answers are proportions and intervals. Evidence: works with proportions.

branches.skill: Standard deviation as typical distance from the mean
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot convert the SD to a margin. Why it matters: the margin is about 2 SDs. Evidence: uses standard deviation.

branches.skill: Plan a sample size for a desired margin of error
branches.new_demand: Reason backward from a desired margin of error to a sample size.

branches.skill: Evaluate reports that use margins of error
branches.new_demand: Use the margin of error to evaluate claims made in reports.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: planned margins of error are used to judge whether reported differences are meaningful.

sets.target_skill: Use a sample mean and the variability of simulated (resampled) means to estimate a population mean with a margin of error, and interpret it

branches.skill: Mean of a data set
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the statistic. Why it matters: the estimate starts from the sample mean. Evidence: computes means.

branches.skill: What resampling simulates
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not understand the simulation. Why it matters: the margin comes from it. Evidence: interprets the simulation.

branches.skill: Two standard deviations and the 95% range
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot form the interval. Why it matters: margin = 2 SD. Evidence: computes the 95% range.

branches.skill: Use intervals to judge claims about a mean
branches.new_demand: Use interval estimates to evaluate claimed values and their scope.

branches.skill: Compare two group means with re-randomization
branches.new_demand: Move from estimating one mean to comparing two treatment means.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: judging a claimed mean against chance variation becomes judging a treatment difference.

sets.target_skill: Use data from a randomized experiment and a supplied re-randomization simulation to decide whether a difference between treatments is significant

branches.skill: Compare the means of two groups
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute the observed difference. Why it matters: the test compares this difference with the simulation. Evidence: compares group means.

branches.skill: Random assignment in experiments
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see why shuffling is valid. Why it matters: re-randomization copies the random assignment. Evidence: explains random assignment.

branches.skill: Probability as relative frequency in simulations
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot convert counts to proportions. Why it matters: significance compares a proportion to a cutoff. Evidence: uses relative frequencies.

branches.skill: Two-sided comparisons and design choices
branches.new_demand: Choose one- or two-sided criteria and reason about how design affects significance.

branches.skill: Evaluate reports of experiments
branches.new_demand: Use the logic of randomized comparisons to evaluate published claims.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: knowing what makes a comparison convincing is applied to outside reports.

sets.target_skill: Evaluate a report based on data by examining the design, the sample, the graph, and whether the conclusion follows

branches.skill: Random samples and bias
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student trusts any sample. Why it matters: evaluation starts with the sample. Evidence: recognizes bias.

branches.skill: Study design and causation
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student accepts causal claims. Why it matters: many reports confuse association and causation. Evidence: connects design and conclusions.

branches.skill: Read scales on graphs
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student is misled by graphs. Why it matters: reports often use graphs. Evidence: reads scales.

branches.skill: Rewrite claims so that they follow from the data
branches.new_demand: Produce accurate claims, not only criticize inaccurate ones.

branches.skill: Analyze decisions based on test results
branches.new_demand: Evaluate claims and decisions that depend on probabilities from tests.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: accurate rewording of claims is applied to medical test claims using probabilities.

sets.target_skill: Decide whether a random procedure is fair (each option equally likely) and design fair procedures with coins, dice, or random numbers

branches.skill: Probabilities of equally likely outcomes
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot assign probabilities. Why it matters: fairness compares probabilities. Evidence: uses equally likely outcomes.

branches.skill: Sample spaces for compound events
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student miscounts outcomes. Why it matters: fairness needs the correct sample space. Evidence: lists sample spaces.

branches.skill: Probability between 0 and 1 and redoing outcomes
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student is confused by "flip again" rules. Why it matters: fair procedures often redo outcomes. Evidence: reasons about probabilities.

branches.skill: Design fair procedures and count expected trials
branches.new_demand: Design fair procedures for awkward numbers of choices and analyze their efficiency.

branches.skill: Analyze strategies and decisions with probability
branches.new_demand: Extend fairness from equal probabilities to expected value in strategies.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: designing equal-chance procedures leads to evaluating games and choices by expected gain.

sets.target_skill: Use probabilities (including conditional reasoning with counts) to analyze decisions such as medical testing, product testing, warranties, and test-taking strategies

branches.skill: Probability of compound independent events
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student adds instead of multiplying. Why it matters: product testing uses independent events. Evidence: multiplies probabilities.

branches.skill: Two-way tables of counts
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot organize the counts. Why it matters: conditional reasoning uses a table. Evidence: builds two-way tables.

branches.skill: Weighted averages of outcomes
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute expected values. Why it matters: decisions compare averages. Evidence: computes weighted sums.

branches.skill: Investigate how changing conditions changes the decision
branches.new_demand: Re-analyze decisions when probabilities or rules change.

branches.skill: Find expected values of random variables
branches.new_demand: Formalize decisions with random variables and expected values (Probability and Statistics).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the repeated what-if decisions are expressed as expected values of random variables.

sets.target_skill: Find the conjugate of a complex number and use it to find the modulus and to write quotients in the form a + bi

branches.skill: Multiply complex numbers
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot multiply by the conjugate. Why it matters: division multiplies by the conjugate. Evidence: multiplies complex numbers.

branches.skill: Distance from the origin
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see the modulus as distance. Why it matters: |a + bi| is the distance to (a, b). Evidence: finds distances.

branches.skill: Powers of i
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student keeps i² terms. Why it matters: conjugate products become real using i² = -1. Evidence: simplifies powers of i.

branches.skill: Prove properties of conjugates and moduli
branches.new_demand: Prove and use general identities for conjugates and moduli.

branches.skill: Write complex numbers in polar form
branches.new_demand: Represent complex numbers by modulus and angle (Precalculus).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the modulus |z| becomes the radius r of the polar form.

sets.target_skill: Identify the graph of a rational function from its zeros, intercepts, vertical and horizontal asymptotes, and end behavior

branches.skill: Rewrite a rational expression by inspection
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the horizontal asymptote. Why it matters: the inspected form shows it. Evidence: rewrites rational expressions.

branches.skill: Domain and excluded values
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misses asymptote locations. Why it matters: vertical asymptotes are at excluded values. Evidence: finds domains.

branches.skill: Sign of a quotient on intervals
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student draws the branches on the wrong side. Why it matters: signs decide the behavior near asymptotes. Evidence: tests signs.

branches.skill: Graph rational functions with slant asymptotes
branches.new_demand: Extend to slant asymptotes and construct functions from features.

branches.skill: Interpret a rational model's features in context
branches.new_demand: Interpret asymptotes and intercepts as quantities in a model.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: constructing functions from asymptotes is reversed into interpreting them.

sets.target_skill: Factor a rational function to identify every hole (with its coordinates) and every vertical asymptote

branches.skill: Factor numerators and denominators
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot see common factors. Why it matters: holes come from canceled common factors. Evidence: factors.

branches.skill: Simplify rational expressions and keep exclusions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student loses the canceled value. Why it matters: the canceled value becomes a hole. Evidence: simplifies and keeps exclusions.

branches.skill: Evaluate the simplified expression
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot locate the hole's height. Why it matters: the hole is at (a, simplified value). Evidence: evaluates.

branches.skill: Construct and graph rational functions with holes
branches.new_demand: Construct functions with prescribed holes and asymptotes and graph them.

branches.skill: Relate holes to extraneous solutions
branches.new_demand: Explain extraneous solutions of rational equations as holes in graphs.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the graph with a hole explains why a solution is missing.

sets.target_skill: Write a composition of two functions, state its domain, and interpret it in context

branches.skill: Build combined models
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student confuses composition with arithmetic. Why it matters: composition is a new way to combine. Evidence: combines functions.

branches.skill: Evaluate a function at an expression
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot substitute an expression. Why it matters: composition substitutes one function into another. Evidence: evaluates at expressions.

branches.skill: Domains of radical, rational, and log functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student omits the composite's domain. Why it matters: the inner output must be a valid input. Evidence: finds domains.

branches.skill: Decompose functions into compositions
branches.new_demand: Reverse composition: decompose a function and compose three functions.

branches.skill: Verify inverses by composition
branches.new_demand: Use composition to test the inverse relationship.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: composing and decomposing functions leads to compositions that give the identity.

sets.target_skill: Verify that two functions are inverses by computing both compositions and checking the domains: identify the complete, correct verification

branches.skill: Find inverses algebraically
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student has no candidate to verify. Why it matters: verification checks a proposed inverse. Evidence: finds inverses.

branches.skill: Compose functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compose. Why it matters: verification is composition. Evidence: composes functions.

branches.skill: Square roots of squares
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student simplifies √(x²) to x. Why it matters: the restriction x ≥ 0 depends on it. Evidence: simplifies √(x²).

branches.skill: Show that proposed inverses fail
branches.new_demand: Use composition to disprove proposed inverses and repair domains.

branches.skill: Read inverse values from tables and graphs
branches.new_demand: Apply the inverse relationship to values in tables and graphs.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: compositions verified algebraically are now checked with tabled values.

sets.target_skill: Read values of f⁻¹ from a table or graph of an invertible function f and interpret them

branches.skill: Inverse functions swap inputs and outputs
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student reads f instead of f⁻¹. Why it matters: reading an inverse means reading backward. Evidence: swaps inputs and outputs.

branches.skill: Read points from graphs and tables
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misreads tables. Why it matters: inverse values are read from the same tables. Evidence: reads functions.

branches.skill: One-to-one functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student reads values from non-invertible data. Why it matters: reading requires one-to-one data. Evidence: recognizes one-to-one functions.

branches.skill: Estimate inverse values between data points and sketch inverse graphs
branches.new_demand: Estimate inverse values between data points and draw inverse graphs.

branches.skill: Restrict the domain to make a function invertible
branches.new_demand: Create invertible functions from non-invertible ones by restricting domains.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: reading inverses needs one-to-one data, which restriction provides.

sets.target_skill: Choose a domain on which a non-invertible function is one-to-one, write the inverse, and state its domain

branches.skill: Find the vertex of a quadratic
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot choose where to split the graph. Why it matters: the restriction starts at the vertex. Evidence: finds vertices.

branches.skill: Write inverses of one-to-one functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student picks the wrong root. Why it matters: the restriction decides the sign of the root. Evidence: solves for x with a restriction.

branches.skill: Domains and ranges
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student omits the inverse's domain. Why it matters: the inverse domain is the range. Evidence: finds ranges.

branches.skill: Compare different restrictions
branches.new_demand: Choose between restrictions and match the restriction to a context.

branches.skill: Restrict trigonometric functions to define inverses
branches.new_demand: Apply domain restriction to periodic functions.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: choosing a monotone piece of a parabola is applied to periodic graphs.

sets.target_skill: Solve logarithmic equations by rewriting them in exponential form (and use log properties), checking for extraneous solutions

branches.skill: Write exact logarithmic solutions of exponential equations
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot convert forms. Why it matters: log equations are solved by converting to exponential form. Evidence: converts between forms.

branches.skill: Check for extraneous solutions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student keeps invalid solutions. Why it matters: log domains reject some candidates. Evidence: checks candidates.

branches.skill: Domains of logarithmic expressions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student ignores the domain. Why it matters: the domain decides extraneous solutions. Evidence: finds log domains.

branches.skill: Use log properties and change of base in equations
branches.new_demand: Combine log properties, change of base, and domain reasoning.

branches.skill: Check logarithmic solutions graphically
branches.new_demand: Use graphs to confirm algebraic solutions and approximate non-algebraic ones.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: domain reasoning about log equations is seen as where the graphs exist and meet.

sets.target_skill: Use special right triangles to find exact values at π/6, π/4, π/3, and use the unit circle to express values at π - x, π + x, and 2π - x in terms of x

branches.skill: Special right triangle side ratios
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the ratios. Why it matters: derivations use the triangles. Evidence: uses special triangles.

branches.skill: Unit-circle values in all quadrants
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot place angles. Why it matters: the relations map angles to the first quadrant. Evidence: finds unit-circle values.

branches.skill: The Pythagorean Theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute the missing side. Why it matters: the derivation needs it. Evidence: uses the Pythagorean Theorem.

branches.skill: Derive more special values and the reflection identities
branches.new_demand: Derive all the special values and prove the reflection relations.

branches.skill: Explain symmetry and periodicity
branches.new_demand: Generalize the reflection relations into odd/even symmetry and periodicity.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the reflection identities combine into symmetry and period statements.

sets.target_skill: Use the unit circle to explain odd/even symmetry and periodicity of sine, cosine, and tangent, and use them to evaluate

branches.skill: Explain the unit-circle definition
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot use the definition. Why it matters: explanations rest on it. Evidence: uses the unit circle.

branches.skill: Even and odd functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student lacks the definitions. Why it matters: symmetry statements use them. Evidence: defines even and odd.

branches.skill: Reflect points over the axes
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot describe the motions. Why it matters: symmetry and periodicity are motions of the circle. Evidence: reflects and rotates points.

branches.skill: Use periodicity and symmetry to evaluate and simplify
branches.new_demand: Combine periodicity and symmetry to evaluate and simplify.

branches.skill: Restrict trigonometric functions so they have inverses
branches.new_demand: Use periodicity and symmetry to justify domain restrictions for inverses.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: periodicity, which repeats values, is exactly what the restriction removes.

sets.target_skill: State and justify the restricted domains for sine, cosine, and tangent, and evaluate inverse trigonometric functions on them

branches.skill: Restrict a domain to make a function invertible
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know why restrictions are made. Why it matters: the trig case uses the same idea. Evidence: restricts domains.

branches.skill: Exact values on the unit circle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot evaluate inverses exactly. Why it matters: inverse values are exact angles. Evidence: knows exact values.

branches.skill: Periodicity of trigonometric functions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see repetition. Why it matters: repetition is why restriction is needed. Evidence: uses periodicity.

branches.skill: Compose trigonometric functions with their inverses
branches.new_demand: Track how the restricted domain affects compositions with inverses.

branches.skill: Solve trigonometric equations with inverses
branches.new_demand: Use inverse values plus symmetry to find all solutions in an interval.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: knowing that inverses return one restricted angle leads to recovering the others.

sets.target_skill: Solve trigonometric equations, including model equations, with inverse functions, and find all solutions in a given interval

branches.skill: Evaluate inverse trigonometric functions on restricted domains
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot get the first solution. Why it matters: inverses give one solution. Evidence: evaluates inverses.

branches.skill: Parameters of sinusoidal models
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot isolate the trig part. Why it matters: model equations need it first. Evidence: reads and rearranges models.

branches.skill: Symmetry of unit-circle solutions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student finds only one solution. Why it matters: all solutions in the interval are required. Evidence: uses symmetry.

branches.skill: Find all real solutions and solve equations that factor
branches.new_demand: Find general solutions and solve equations that factor or involve squares and multiple angles.

branches.skill: Solve equations with sum and double-angle identities
branches.new_demand: Use addition and double-angle identities (Precalculus) to solve equations.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: factoring trig equations is extended with identities that create factorable forms.
